changes.old: Added by /shape-slice for bi-788 (ontology v9 and v10, ADR 049): a business intent has one plan, and never a second; the plan's ID is the intent's issue number. The plan holds every slice that serves its intent, found from the link "slice serves business intent", and it takes the slice that was shaped; it does not pick or test slices. For each slice it makes one epic, or uses the one that exists, and one story for each feature of the slice. A story's scope of work holds the goal, the limits and the expectations from its feature's ICE and that feature's capability's ICE, and its Context guidance is its own property. A story never holds a failure condition. The plan play does not write the slice's hidden file; /shape-slice writes it (decision 6 of #844, recorded in ADR 052, which amends ADR 049 Decisions 1.2 and 4). The product owner agreed on 2026-10-24 (#844) to change the old words "a tracker issue for every node" to this rule: under ontology v7 and later a capability and a feature get no tracker issue; only the epic and the stories do.

changes.old: This capability takes in the old capability Link the product model, filed under the closed intent bi-722 (A product model can be managed, and grows as plans are built). Its old page said that "work can start before the model is complete, if the model links its parts by these rules". Its ready check is built; its link check and its search by domain are not. Three of its features stay here, with their ids and their folders, each rewritten to what was built: fn-724 is the ready check, fn-725 the links between parts, and fn-726 the list of what serves an intent and what sits in a domain. Its fourth feature, fn-597, the ontology itself, belongs to Define what a product is made of.
